name: Apple Pay on the web (ApplePaySession)
plain: Pays with Apple Pay in Safari or via the Payment Request API.
meaning: The site gets a payment token, billing and shipping contact only after Face ID or Touch ID approval.

access.prompt_ui: Apple Pay sheet with Face ID, Touch ID or passcode
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Pays with Apple Pay in Safari or via the Payment Request API.

limits.headline: Can start an Apple Pay payment that you confirm with Face ID or Touch ID
limits.user_action: You tap the Apple Pay button at checkout.
can: Show the Apple Pay sheet with your cards and shipping address
Send a one time payment code to the store after you approve
Ask for your name, email or phone if you choose to share them
cannot: Charge you without Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode
Use Apple Pay in Chrome, Edge or Firefox
Keep your details for later; each payment needs a new approval
limits.differs: Safari on iPhone and Mac supports it directly. Chrome, Edge and Firefox use other wallets.

story.what_it_is: Pay in Safari with Apple Pay, confirmed by Face ID or Touch ID.

marketing.name: Apple Pay on the Web
marketing.pitch: Apple says Apple Pay lets customers check out quickly and securely on websites in Safari.

story.for_you: You tap the Apple Pay button, check the total, and approve with your face or finger. The shop gets a payment token, not your card number.
story.for_makers: Makers get higher checkout completion and fewer card number worries. It also gives them your shipping contact once you approve.

use_cases.example: You pay for shoes on a store site with one tap and no typing.
A booking site lets you pay for a flight with Face ID.
A food order site finishes checkout in one tap.
A ticket seller confirms your purchase and sends the tickets to your phone.
A fraud team sees the Apple Pay token and trusts it more than a typed card number.
A news site sells a subscription with one tap.

technical_bounds: Needs merchant validation and a registered domain
